security_spec.violation_condition: In KVM, when HS-mode enables CLIC fast interrupts (selected interrupt files configured with Smip-style hardware save/restore) while the hart is executing in VS/VU-mode, the hardware unconditionally saves x10-x15 onto the guest's stack. If the guest stack pointer (sp) is malicious, unmapped, or misaligned, the hardware save triggers a fault at a point where the hypervisor cannot safely recover, or silently corrupts guest memory that the hypervisor relies on for paravirtualized state.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: KVM CLIC interrupt enablement paths where guest stack pointer validity is not verified before allowing hardware register save to the guest-owned stack during VS/VU-mode execution — grep for CLIC/Smip interrupt file configuration combined with KVM guest entry/exit paths (kvm_riscv_vcpu_enter, __kvm_riscv_switch_to, clic interrupt routing)
affected_entities: CLIC interrupt files configured for Smip fast interrupt handling
hardware-implicit sp (stack pointer used for x10-x15 save/restore)
security_spec.summary: Removal of conditional stack swap (cspspush/cspspop) from CLIC fast interrupt entry/exit means the hardware now unconditionally saves registers onto the interrupted context's stack; in KVM this is the guest-controlled stack pointer, creating a data corruption surface if the hypervisor does not ensure guest sp validity before enabling fast interrupts during guest execution.

findings.finding: No CLIC/Smip fast interrupt configuration exists anywhere in this kernel. The guest entry path performs pure software context switch via __kvm_riscv_switch_to() (or __kvm_riscv_nacl_switch_to()), saving/restoring registers through the kvm_vcpu_arch structure, not via hardware stack save. There is no code that enables selective interrupt files or configures hardware auto-save of x10-x15 to the guest stack pointer.

The low-level switch_to() implementation is a conventional software context switch: SAVE_HOST_GPRS → SAVE_HOST_AND_RESTORE_GUEST_CSRS → RESTORE_GUEST_GPRS → sret. All GPRs (including x10-x15/a0-a5) are explicitly saved to and restored from the kvm_vcpu_arch structure in memory. There is no reliance on or configuration of hardware stack-based register save as described in the Smip/CLIC spec. The guest SP loaded at line 68 is under full KVM control and only used for guest execution after sret, not for interrupt-time hardware saves.
findings.snippet:
SAVE_HOST_GPRS
SAVE_HOST_AND_RESTORE_GUEST_CSRS .Lkvm_switch_return
RESTORE_GUEST_GPRS
/* Resume Guest using SRET */
sret

findings.finding: VCPU load path configures only standard CSRs (VSSTATUS, VSIE, VSTVEC, VSSCRATCH, VSEPC, VSCAUSE, VSTVAL, HEDELEG, HVIP, VSATP, HENVCFG, HSTATEEN0) via either NACL or direct CSR writes. No CLIC-related CSRs (e.g., mintstatus, mnxti, cliccfg) are touched. Interrupt configuration is exclusively through the standard AIA (IMSIC/APLIC) model via kvm_riscv_vcpu_aia_load().

The main VCPU run loop has no guest stack pointer validation before entering the guest because the Smip hardware save feature is not implemented. The interrupt flushing/syncing (kvm_riscv_vcpu_flush_interrupts, kvm_riscv_update_hvip) operates entirely through standard HVIP/VSIE CSRs and AIA high interrupts. No CLIC interrupt file configuration or mnxti-based fast interrupt delivery path exists.
